Description: explicit — route shields missing badge on the open OpenMapTiles stack
prompt: I'm using an open OpenMapTiles / OSM-based vector basemap with MapLibre GL JS (no Mapbox account). My interstate and US highway shields render as bare floating numbers with no shield badge behind them; the numbers are fine. My tiles do populate network, ref, and ref_length. Which exact sprite image names do the shield layers expect, and how do I get the badges to appear without editing the layers?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
### What the shield layers are looking for

All three OSM-based “shield” layers (interstate, US-highway, US-state) use the **same naming convention**:

```text
icon-image: "{network}_{ref_length}"
```

* `network` – the value that comes from the tile source (`us-interstate`, `us-highway`, `us-state` or the generic `road` for non-US routes).  
* `ref_length` – the length of the `ref` string (the number of characters in the road number). The style creates this field for you (`ref_length = stringLength(ref)`).

So the **exact sprite IDs** that the style will try to fetch are:

| Network (tile field) | Sprite IDs that may be requested |
|----------------------|----------------------------------|
| `us-interstate`      | `us-interstate_1`, `us-interstate_2`, `us-interstate_3`, … up to the longest interstate number your sprite contains (OSM Bright: 1-3, OpenMapTiles v3+: 1-5) |
| `us-highway`         | `us-highway_1`, `us-highway_2`, `us-highway_3` |
| `us-state`           | `us-state_1`, `us-state_2`, `us-state_3`, `us-state_4`, `us-state_5`, `us-state_6` |
| `road` (any other network) | `road_1`, `road_2`, `road_3`, `road_4`, `road_5`, `road_6` |

If the sprite you are using does **not** contain the ID that matches the current `network` + `ref_length`, the layer can still draw the text (the number) but the badge image is missing – exactly the “bare floating numbers” you are seeing.

---

## How to get the badges without touching the style layers

You have three practical ways to supply the missing images. All of them keep the existing layer definitions (`icon-image: "{network}_{ref_length}"`) untouched.

### 1. Point the style at a sprite that already contains those IDs  

The easiest solution is to use a sprite that ships the full set of shield images.

| Source | Sprite URL (base, **no** extension) | What it contains |
|--------|--------------------------------------|------------------|
| **OpenMapTiles / OSM Bright (official)** | `https://openmaptiles.github.io/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite` | All `us-interstate_*`, `us-highway_*`, `us-state_*`, `road_*` up to the lengths shown in the table above. |
| **MapLibre demo style** | `https://demotiles.maplibre.org/styles/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite` | Same content as the official OSM Bright sprite (good for testing, **not** for production). |

**Steps**

1. **Copy the sprite files** (`*.png`, `*.json`, and any `@2x` variants) to a location you control (same origin as your app, or a CDN with proper CORS headers).  
2. **Edit the style’s `sprite` property** to point at that base URL, e.g.:

   ```json
   {
     "sprite": "https://mycdn.example.com/sprites/osm-bright"
   }
   ```

   *Do not add “.png” or “.json” – MapLibre adds those automatically.*

3. Reload the map. The shield badges will now be found and rendered.

> **Why this works:** The style already asks for `us-interstate_2`, `us-highway_3`, etc. When the sprite JSON contains those keys, `map.hasImage(id)` returns `true` and the badge is drawn.

---

### 2. Add a **second sprite sheet** to the style (MapLibre ≥ 3.0)

If you already have a custom sprite (e.g., your own POI icons) and you don’t want to merge the shield images into it, you can keep the existing sheet and **add a second one** that only holds the shield badges.

**Style JSON**

```json
{
  "sprite": [
    { "id": "default", "url": "https://mycdn.example.com/sprites/my-poi" },
    { "id": "shields", "url": "https://mycdn.example.com/sprites/osm-bright" }
  ]
}
```

**How to reference the images**

* Prefix the image name with the sheet id: `"icon-image": "shields:us-interstate_2"`  
* **BUT** you *don’t* have to change any layer definitions if you give the shield sheet the id **`default`**.  
  *Rename the existing custom sheet to something else (e.g., `"my-poi"`), and make the shield sheet the `default` entry:

    ```json
    {
      "sprite": [
        { "id": "my-poi", "url": "https://mycdn.example.com/sprites/my-poi" },
        { "id": "default", "url": "https://mycdn.example.com/sprites/osm-bright" }
      ]
    }
    ```

  *Now the original layer expressions (`"{network}_{ref_length}"`) resolve automatically against the `default` sheet, and you keep your POI icons in the other sheet.

**Adding the sheet at runtime (optional)**  

If you cannot edit the style file (e.g., you receive it from a third-party), you can add the extra sheet after the map loads:

```js
map.on('style.load', () => {
  map.addSprite('shields', 'https://mycdn.example.com/sprites/osm-bright');
});
```

Again, give the shield sheet the id `default` (or rename the existing one) to avoid any prefix changes.

---

### 3. Register the missing images **programmatically** with `addImage`

When you cannot change the `sprite` URL at all (e.g., you are using a hosted style you cannot edit), you can supply the missing badge images yourself after the map has loaded.

```js
async function addShieldImages() {
  const networks = ['us-interstate', 'us-highway', 'us-state', 'road'];
  const maxLengths = {
    'us-interstate': 5,   // OpenMapTiles provides up to 5
    'us-highway': 3,
    'us-state': 6,
    'road': 6
  };

  for (const net of networks) {
    const max = maxLengths[net];
    for (let len = 1; len <= max; len++) {
      const id = `${net}_${len}`;
      if (map.hasImage(id)) continue;               // already present
      const url = `https://mycdn.example.com/shields/${id}.png`; // your own copy
      const { data } = await map.loadImage(url);
      map.addImage(id, data);
    }
  }
}

map.on('load', addShieldImages);
```

*You must host the individual PNG (or WebP) files yourself.*  
If you have the original sprite JSON, you can extract each image from the PNG atlas (many tools exist – e.g., `spritezero` can also output the individual PNGs) and serve them individually.

**Pros:** No style changes, works even with a read-only style URL.  
**Cons:** One HTTP request per badge (unless you bundle them with a service worker or HTTP/2 multiplexing).

---

## Quick checklist – get the badges back in minutes

1. **Verify the missing IDs**  
   ```js
   console.log('Missing shields:', ['us-interstate_2','us-highway_3','us-state_5']
               .filter(id => !map.hasImage(id)));
   ```
2. **Pick one of the three approaches**  
   * **Replace the sprite URL** with a full OSM Bright sprite (recommended).  
   * **Add a second sprite sheet** (default id = shields) if you need to keep your own icons separate.  
   * **Programmatically add the images** with `addImage` if you cannot touch the style at all.
3. **Make sure CORS is correct** – the sprite JSON/PNG (or the individual PNGs) must be served with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` (or your domain).  
4. **Reload the map** – the shield badges should now appear behind the numbers.

---

### TL;DR – exact image names you need

```
us-interstate_1
us-interstate_2
us-interstate_3
us-interstate_4   (if your sprite provides it)
us-interstate_5   (if your sprite provides it)

us-highway_1
us-highway_2
us-highway_3

us-state_1
us-state_2
us-state_3
us-state_4
us-state_5
us-state_6

road_1
road_2
road_3
road_4
road_5
road_6
```

If any of those IDs are missing from the sprite that your style loads, the corresponding shield badge will be invisible. Point the style at a sprite that contains **all** of the IDs above (or add them via a second sheet or `addImage`) and the shields will render correctly without any layer edits.
